msg: @font-face serves a foundry family that is almost never covered by a desktop purchase - a separate webfont licence is normally required before this file ships
A .ttf/.otf/.eot binary is served to browsers from @font-face - desktop EULAs commonly licence those formats for installed use only
Font binary is base64-embedded in the stylesheet - several foundry EULAs name embedding and re-distribution of the binary as a separate grant
An SIL OFL family is shipped under a modified name - the Reserved Font Name clause forbids keeping the original name on a modified or re-hinted build
Remote Google Fonts request sends the visitor IP address to a third country - the ground that LG Muenchen I decided in case 3 O 17493/20 on 2022-01-20
Adobe Fonts kit is loaded remotely - that licence is bound to the domains listed in the kit, so a new domain or a self-hosted copy is out of scope
MyFonts pageview counter is present - the webfont licence is metered by pageview, so traffic growth silently moves the tier
Font Awesome Pro asset is referenced - Pro is a per-seat paid plan and its kit token must not sit in a public repository
Font is pulled from a third-party CDN - the served binary and its licence terms are outside your build and can change without notice
The stylesheet declares @font-face but carries no licence line - an audit letter asks for the licence covering each served family
An SIL OFL family is served but the OFL notice is not in this file - the licence requires the copyright and permission notice to travel with the font
Licence or foundry reference uses plain http - the linked terms cannot be shown to have been unmodified in transit
